text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- European Union finance ministers have agreed that Danes are to be allowed to import alcohol and tobacco after being 24 hours abroad compared to the present 36 hour rule. The new 24 hour rule is to remain in effect until end-2003.
--- Danish information technology firms are having trouble finding local qualified multi-media staff and may have to move abroad taking jobs with them in a growth industry.
--- Common European Union rules to be introduced in 1997 will make it impossible for Denmark to maintain its demand for a compulsory marking system for genetically-engineered food in retail stores.

--- Danish exporters expect sales to Britain to increase by almost 10 percent in 1996, more than two billion crowns up on last year, due to a 15 percent rise in the value of the pound sterling this year and expected U.K. economic growth of 3.5 percent next year.

--- Danish environmental and energy minister Svend Auken's recent stop on the building of new shopping malls was decreed without legal authority according an Aarhus University report. Retailers, contractors and local authorities are expected to lodge complaints about the ban with the parliamentary ombudsman.
